$comment: WHAT MAY LEAVE THIS MACHINE FOR THE PRIVATE CLOUD MIRROR OF THE APP REPOSITORY.
READ BY the engine's src/lib/cloud-agent/cloud-mirror.js. Nothing is sent unless
a rule here selects it, and a tracked path that matches no rule at all REFUSES
the publish by name (CLOUD_MIRROR_UNCLASSIFIED) rather than being sent or
silently skipped.
THIS IS NOT config/payload-boundary.json. That file answers whether something
may be published PUBLICLY under the open-source licence; this one answers
whether it may leave this machine into a PRIVATE repository that a cloud agent
clones. The two questions have genuinely different answers and are kept apart on
purpose. The mechanism, the vocabulary and the fail-closed rules are the same so
that the two are READ the same way.
WHY THIS REPOSITORY IS THE URGENT ONE, MEASURED 2026-08-24. Cloud agents working
on this repository were diffing against origin/packaging/capability-layer, which
is 467 commits behind local HEAD (origin/main is 756 behind). Their harvests came
back as empty applies, as 'fixes' already present in the tree, and as citations
pointing at unrelated code. The engine's branch is 5 behind and its harvests were
clean the same night. That correlation is the whole diagnosis, and this manifest
is what lets the current tree be sent instead.
ROOT-LEVEL FILES ARE NAMED EXACTLY AND DELIBERATELY, and this repository is the
reason the rule is worth its cost: the root is where a stray instruction or
account-specific file lands. A new one stops the publish until somebody reads
and classifies that exact path.
Everything a cloud agent needs to read, build, test and change the app.
FOUR OF THESE PREFIXES ARE EXCLUDED BY config/payload-boundary.json's
source.excluded -- auxiliary/, reports/, docs/coordinator/, and retained root
reports -- AND MIRRORING THEM IS A DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE,
not an oversight. They are excluded there because they are internal working
material that should not appear in a public open-source publish. A private
mirror is exactly where current internal source and retained provenance belong.
Current authority comes from AGENTS.md and the active task, never a historical
brief. The one class this manifest and that one AGREE on is private/, which
is the owner's own data rather than the project's -- and it is withheld
below.
private/ is the one directory in this tree named for what it is, and its own
files say so. private/fleet-profile.owner.json calls itself 'the fleet the
product was built against, preserved verbatim', with the owner's machines and
their addresses in it. private/research-queue.authored.json holds owner
observations transcribed as provenance, and the app's own ledger doctrine
treats his verbatim words as an authority -- which is exactly the material
that should not be handed to a third-party-hosted worker to read.
NOTHING IN THE TREE REQUIRES EITHER FILE. Both are loaded by hand at runtime
(the profile's own note gives the localStorage.setItem line a person types),
and each is deliberately outside public/ and outside build.files so that
neither vite nor electron-builder can pack it. A clone of the mirror without
them builds and tests identically.

credentialScanAcknowledged.$comment: Not read as rules. A key here is a path or directory prefix; a value is why credential-SHAPED text is expected there.
credentialScanAcknowledged.tools/test/: Test fixtures deliberately carry credential-SHAPED strings so the scrubbers and refusal paths have something realistic to be tested against. Measured 2026-08-24: 7 files under this prefix match the detector, every one an obvious fixture whose own value says so -- their tails read ...would-bill, ...must-never-be-echoed, ...shouldneverbeused. The heads are deliberately NOT quoted here: this file is scanned like any other, and quoting a full provider prefix made it refuse its own mirror publish twice. THE HOLE IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: this covers the whole prefix, so a real credential committed under tools/test/ would not be caught by the content scan. The vault discipline and the classification above are what stand there.
credentialScanAcknowledged.tools/subscribe-page-drive.mjs: A page driver that posts a fixed Paddle TEST-mode key (a Paddle TEST-mode key whose own tail reads ...drivenbyharness; the head is not spelled here because this file is scanned like any other) to the local subscribe endpoint so the checkout surface can be exercised without a live transaction. It is a harness value authored in the file, not a key for any account.
